- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh: line 619 — `worktree_obj = git("hash-object", "--", path).decode().strip()` inside `_assert_index_transition_allowed`
  PROBLEM: `git hash-object -- <path>` follows symlinks: it opens the target file's content, not the link text. But `git ls-files -z --stage` (used by `index_entries()` at line 563 to produce `staged_obj`) stores the symlink's blob, which contains the link text. For a symlink conflicted path, `staged_obj` (hash of link text, mode 120000) will never equal `worktree_obj` (hash of target file content, mode 100644), so the check `worktree_obj != staged_obj` at line 622 is always true for symlinks, raising `ValueError("allowed path staged content does not match the resolved worktree")` and failing the action closed (exit 2).
  WHY: `workflow-templates/CLAUDE.md` is a real symlink to `../CLAUDE.md` in this repo (confirmed by `tests/test_touched_set_symlink_aware.py:83` and documented at `tests/test_touched_set_symlink_aware.py:1-11`). It is a common conflicted path during main-merge resolutions (PR #4443, runs 36101772827–36120214576). When the model stages this symlink, `_assert_index_transition_allowed` calls `git hash-object -- workflow-templates/CLAUDE.md`, which follows the link and hashes `CLAUDE.md`'s content. The staged blob from `git ls-files --stage` is the hash of the link text `../CLAUDE.md`. The mismatch triggers `ValueError`, the `check` action exits 2, and the resolver aborts — identical to the pre-fix behavior for regular files.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
